module_title: Formation of INC and the Moderate Phase (1885-1905) - Basics
introduction: The foundation of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885 marked the beginning of an organized national movement. The period from 1885 to 1905 is known as the 'Moderate Phase'. The leaders of this phase believed in peaceful and constitutional methods to demand political and administrative reforms from the British.

core_concepts.title: Foundation of INC
core_concepts.description: The Indian National Congress was founded on December 28, 1885, by Allan Octavian Hume (A.O. Hume), a retired British civil servant.

core_concepts.title: The First Session
core_concepts.description: The first session of the INC was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay (Mumbai), attended by 72 delegates from all over India.

core_concepts.title: Moderate Ideology
core_concepts.description: Moderate leaders had deep faith in the British sense of justice. They used constitutional and peaceful methods like petitions, prayers, and meetings to put forward their demands.

core_concepts.title: Key Demands
core_concepts.description: Their main demands included the expansion of legislative councils, employment of Indians in higher civil service posts, and a reduction in military expenditure.

core_concepts.title: Viceroy during Formation
core_concepts.description: Lord Dufferin was the Viceroy of India when the Indian National Congress was established.

important_entities.name: A.O. Hume
important_entities.significance: Brought various regional Indian leaders together on a single all-India political platform.

important_entities.name: W.C. Bonnerjee
important_entities.significance: Presided over the historic first session of the Congress in Bombay in 1885.

important_entities.name: Dadabhai Naoroji
important_entities.significance: One of the most prominent moderate leaders who became the Congress President three times.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse A.O. Hume as the first president. Hume was the founder and General Secretary, but the first President was W.C. Bonnerjee.
The first session was originally scheduled to be held in Poona (Pune), but it was shifted to Bombay due to an outbreak of cholera.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: This summarizes the working method of the moderate leaders: they prayed to the British, filed petitions, and protested peacefully.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize the foundation year (1885), location (Bombay), and the number of attending delegates (72).
Questions frequently ask who the Viceroy was during the formation of the INC (Answer: Lord Dufferin).
